title: ManaSearch Real-Card Mechanical Benchmark
methodology: Deterministic offline fixtures transcribed from linked MTG card reference pages. Each URL points to an online Oracle-text reference. Tests run the production ManaSearch parser, repeatability annotator, mechanic-profile builder, and mechanical scorer; no Scryfall requests are made during test runs.
sourcesNote: Card text and card identities were reviewed against the linked card reference pages. Source links are provided per fixture for maintenance and manual review.

pairs.purpose: Similar tap abilities that produce different amounts of colorless mana.
Both are two-mana-accelerating rocks, but colorless output differs from color fixing.
Two blink effects using different but equivalent wording.
Blink versus exile removal; the returned creature is not left exiled.
Both are token-creation replacement effects; Doubling Season also changes counters.
Token multiplication is not the same as a spell creating tokens.
Both change counter placement via replacement effects, with different scopes and outcomes.
Both repeatedly sacrifice a creature as a cost to produce mana.
Shared repeatable sacrifice outlet structure, different outcomes (mana versus damage).
Both are one-shot spells that sacrifice a permanent as an additional cost and draw two cards; Deadly Dispute also makes a Treasure.
Both are repeatable triggered card-draw engines with different triggering events.
Repeatable spell-cast trigger versus a single conditional ETB draw.
Recurring upkeep draw versus recurring opponent-spell trigger draw.
Card draw after a creature dies versus a one-shot spell with a sacrifice cost.
Both trigger damage to each opponent when creatures enter under your control.
Counter any spell versus countering noncreature spells only.
Countering a spell versus destroying an on-board nonartifact creature.
Both return a creature card from graveyard to battlefield, with different costs and Aura attachment behavior.
Battlefield reanimation versus returning a card to hand.
Exile removal with life compensation versus destroy removal with an artifact restriction.
Card-draw replacement effect versus a triggered ability that may draw a card.
Graveyard-to-library recovery and graveyard reshuffling versus graveyard-to-battlefield reanimation.
